platform.explanation: 3D-printed microfluidic device with patient-derived multicellular spheroids

readout.explanation: Primary ex vivo readout is viability reduction, plus spheroid area change

direction.explanation: Higher viability reduction correlates with clinical responsiveness

threshold_rule.explanation: No binary classification rule specified, only trend correlations

patient_mapping.explanation: Each patient (T1-T10) has linked clinical data and ex vivo results

regimen_match.explanation: Difficult to correlate patient treatment regimens directly with ex vivo experiments

n_units.explanation: 10 patient samples included in the clinical correlation analysis

split.explanation: No independent test cohort, entire 10-patient cohort used for correlation

headline.blocked_reason: No global clinical/toxicity headline (e.g. accuracy, sensitivity, AUC) reported; only qualitative positive correlations and case examples are provided, no aggregate performance metric.

notes: The paper reports qualitative correlations between ex vivo spheroid viability reduction and clinical outcomes, but no single aggregate headline performance metric (e.g. accuracy, AUC) for clinical prediction.
